During the creative process, Pixel3D App not only helps you exercise your intelligence and spatial imagination, but also serves as a great tool for stress relief, entertainment, and killing time. As you immerse yourself in the joy of drawing pixel art, you will unconsciously forget about troubles and stress, enjoying the pleasure brought by creation. It's worth mentioning that the conversion of pixel art into 3D models by Pixel3D App yields stunning results. You can witness the transformation of your work from a flat pixel drawing into a threedimensional and vivid 3D model, which undoubtedly brings you a great sense of achievement. This magical transformation constantly brings surprises to you during the creative process. In conclusion, the Pixel3D App app is an imaginative and creative pixel drawing board tool that makes pixel art creation even more interesting and vivid. If you are also passionate about pixel art, then give this app a try. [pyproject.toml](/tamnd/riemannhandbook/blob/main/pyproject.toml "pyproject.toml") View all files Repository files navigation The Riemann Handbook A book, in PDF and EPUB, that writes the Lean proof of the Riemann Hypothesis in [tamnd/riemannlean](https://github.com/tamnd/riemannlean) as mathematics: definitions, theorems, lemmas and their proofs, in words. The claim is not checked. Nobody has built the Lean project in full yet, and no person has checked the written statements against the Lean code. This book explains the Lean code. It is not a separate check of the mathematics. See [What is checked](https://riemann.tamnd.com/trust/). The volumes Volume Source 0 Guide: how to read, the status of the claim, notation, the named results, the index of Lean names content/front/ and tamnd/riemann 1 Background: the mathematics that the proof uses, in 17 chapters the Learn pages of tamnd/riemann 2 The proof: the top of the proof, its chapters and steps the written proof of tamnd/riemann 3 to 12 The Lean development, one branch or one Lean folder in each volume content/dev/, written for this book The books are in the [releases](https://github.com/tamnd/riemannhandbook/releases). The plan of the development volumes Each declaration of the proof is inside the dominated subtree of exactly one other declaration (its immediate dominator, in the graph of uses from riemannHypothesis). The ledger gives an entry to each declaration whose dominated subtree is large, in tiers: 1,000 or more declarations (591 entries), 300 or more (1,927), 100 or more (5,764). It assigns each entry to a volume by its branch of the proof or by its Lean folder, and to a chapter by its Lean folder. In a chapter, the entries come from the top of the proof down. python m rhb ledger records /path/to/records min 1000 write ledger/coverage.md has the numbers. prompts/entry.md is the brief for the writers of entries. Build You need Python 3.11 or later, [pandoc](https://pandoc.org) 3.8 or later and [Tectonic](https://tectonictypesetting.github.io). Put tamnd/riemann and tamnd/riemannlean next to this repository. pip install . python m rhb survey python m rhb check python m rhb build volume 0,1,2 formats pdf,epub The books go to build/. The pipeline is that of [The Handbook of Algorithms](https://github.com/tamnd/algorithmhandbook): Markdown, then pandoc with filters/rhb.lua, then LaTeX with tex/handbook.sty, then Tectonic. The EPUB is EPUB 3 with MathML. Licence The text is licensed under [CC BY 4.0](/tamnd/riemannhandbook/blob/main/LICENSECONTENT), as the text of tamnd/riemann. The builder is licensed under the [MIT licence](/tamnd/riemannhandbook/blob/main/LICENSE). Please report errors at [issues](https://github.com/tamnd/riemannhandbook/issues). items.title: Show HN: Vouch – See what AI assistants say about your brand mid-conversation
items.desc: description: Vouch is a generative engine optimisation tool that shows how AI assistants talk about your brand across a whole buying conversation, and where you drop out. title: AI search visibility across the whole conversation image: https://vouchgeo.com/opengraphimage.png [Skip to content](main) What happens _after_ the prompt. Vouch is a generative engine optimisation (GEO) tool that shows brands how AI assistants talk about them across a whole buying conversation, and where they drop out. AI search does not end at the first answer: buyers ask five more questions, and that is where your brand wins or disappears. [Join the waitlist](/signup)[See a sample Thread](samplethread) Inviteonly for now. Every invitation starts with a 14day free trial. Assistants tracked today: Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, Perplexity (API answers), Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode and Copilot (Bing AI answer). Threads run on 4 of the 7 (Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT and Perplexity (API answers)). What you see in Vouch The dashboard leads with the week’s Vouch Rate. Open any Thread to read the conversation question by question and see the stage where your brand dropped out. Example data The project dashboard: what changed this week, the Vouch Rate and where buyers drop the brand, ahead of the salvation rate, visibility, share of voice and position. Example data from the builtin demo brand Demo Cycles, not a real customer. Example data A Thread run: the brand is named for three questions, then drops out at the Trust stage. Example data from the builtin demo brand Demo Cycles, not a real customer. See what happens after the prompt A oneminute tour, with a voiceover and captions. Your browser cannot play this video. [Download it](/demo/vouchdemo.mp4) or read the transcript below. Example data from the builtin demo brand Demo Cycles, not a real customer. Read the transcript Ask ChatGPT for the best running shoes for marathon training, and your brand might make the first answer. But buyers don’t stop at one question. They ask which is lighter. Which lasts longer. Which is better value. And by the third followup, your brand is gone. Here’s the thing. Vouch shows you exactly where that happens. It asks the questions your buyers ask, across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity and more, and follows the conversation through every turn. So you see your Vouch Rate, right next to every competitor, week by week. You see the exact answer where you dropped out, and why. And you get clear fixes, plus a report you can share with your team. So, stop guessing what happens after the prompt. Try Vouch free, at vouchgeo.com. People don’t ask the AI one question. They have a conversation. Most tools check whether your brand is mentioned in the first answer. Buyers keep asking: for a shortlist, the downsides, whether to trust you, whether you are worth the price, and which one to buy. You can be named first and still lose the sale four questions later. Singleprompt tracking compared with a ThreadSingleprompt tracking records one answer: named or not. A Thread records six answers and shows the stage where the brand drops out and which rival is chosen.Singleprompt trackingBest electric cycles under 50,000?Your brand: NamedOne answerNamed or not. The conversationthat follows is never seen.A Vouch Thread1\. DiscoveryNamed2\. ShortlistNamed3\. ObjectionNamed4\. TrustDropped5\. ValueNot named6\. DecisionRival chosenSix answersWhere you drop out, and who replaced you. Singleprompt tracking sees one answer. A Thread sees the whole conversation, so it shows where a brand drops out and who takes its place. How Threads work A Thread is one buyer’s conversation with an AI assistant, six questions long. Vouch asks your tracked prompt, then follows up the way a buyer would, and records where your brand is named at each stage. Vouch writes the followup questions for your category; these are examples. 1. Stage 1 Discovery What are the best electric cycles under 50,000? 2. Stage 2 Shortlist Compare the top three for daily commuting. 3. Stage 3 Objection What are the downsides of the first one? 4. Stage 4 Trust Is their aftersales service reliable? 5. Stage 5 Value Is it worth the price over the others? 6. Stage 6 Decision Which one should I buy, and where? The six stages of a ThreadA buyer conversation moves through Discovery, Shortlist, Objection, Trust, Value and Decision. In this example the brand is named for the first three questions and dropped at Trust, when the buyer asks whether the brand can be trusted.One buyer conversation, six questionsStage 1DiscoveryBest options?Stage 2ShortlistCompare threeStage 3ObjectionDownsides?Stage 4TrustReliable?Stage 5ValueWorth it?Stage 6DecisionWhich to buy?Dropped hereExample: your brand is named for three questions,then a rival takes its place when the buyer asks about trust. A Thread follows one buyer through six questions. Being named in the first answer is not being chosen: a brand can drop out later, at Objection or Trust. A sample Thread Sample Four brands start the conversation. One gets the sale. Here your brand survives Discovery, Shortlist and Objection, then drops out at Trust, when the buyer asks about aftersales service. Sample data, not a real brand. Your brand in this sample 1. Discovery 2. Shortlist 3. Objection 4. TrustDropped 5. Value 6. Decision The Vouch Rate The Vouch Rate is one number from 0 to 100: how far your brand survives in the conversation, and whether the assistant recommends you at the end. Vouch shows it only when at least 2 conversations completed that week. [How the Vouch Rate is scored](/methodologyscore) How the Vouch Rate is madeEach conversation scores from 0 to 1: half for how many of the six stages the brand survives, half for being recommended at the end, and sentiment moves the score by up to a tenth. The Vouch Rate is the week’s average times 100.Stages survivedHalfDepth of mention: 0 to 6 stagesChosen at the endHalfThe final answer recommends youSentimentUp to a tenthWarm

Download, explore files and run it on Hugging Face. title: eltokh7/inkling2minidecision · Hugging Face image: https://cdnthumbnails.huggingface.co/socialthumbnails/models/eltokh7/inkling2minidecision.png [ ](inkling2minidecisioneltokh7inkling2minidecision) Inkling2Mini Decision (eltokh7/inkling2minidecision) [](/eltokh7/inkling2minidecision/blob/main/assets/header.jpg) An openweights System 1.5 adaptivedepth decision model built on [thinkingmachines/Inkling2Mini](https://huggingface.co/thinkingmachines/Inkling2Mini) (26.4B total / 3.4B–5.4B active MoE, 24 physical layers with a 12layer looped core). Instead of generating prose or JSON tokens, it evaluates a state and typed questions (choice, noul, score) in a single forward pass and dynamically decides how many internal loops (1, 2, or 3 \= 24, 36, or 48 logical layers) to spend before answering — with zero reasoning tokens. [ ](keyresults) Key Results Routine decisions (decisionv7/test, $n=1{,}440$): 85.56% accuracy, 0.1944 Brier, 0.0235 ECE — right alongside 27Bdense Kev27B (86.3%) at \~5× lower active prefill FLOPs. Difficultyrouted early exit (τ = 0.90): 54.2% of routine decisionv7 questions exit right after Loop 1 (only 8.8% of hard OOD hardv1 questions do — 76.8% automatically route to Loop 3). Real GPU wallclock speed (merge_and_unload \+ torch.compile, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, median headline / mean in parens): Batch1 Early Exit (τ = 0.90): 81.4 ms median (97.4 ms mean) — 1.68× faster median than compiled Loop 3 (136.8 ms median / 146.3 ms mean) with −0.07 pp accuracy difference (85.49% vs. 85.56%). Batch1 Early Exit (τ = 0.85): 79.6 ms median (95.4 ms mean) — 1.72× faster median. Perpass medians (batch1): 65.6 ms (Loop 1) / 100.2 ms (Loop 2) / 136.8 ms (Loop 3). Batched throughput (bs = 8, causal_conv1d): 27.9 ms/q (35.8 q/s) at Loop 1 and 61.4 ms/q (16.3 q/s) at Loop 3. Latent reasoning on untrained OOD hard tasks (hardv1): Going from Loop 1 → Loop 3 adds +26.8 pp on hardv1/dev (39.9% → 66.7%) and +24.3 pp on hardv1/test (42.6% → 66.8%), beating 9Bdense Kev9B v1 (58.2% / 58.4%) by +8.4 pp with 5.4B active parameters. [](/eltokh7/inkling2minidecision/blob/main/assets/hard%5Fv1%5Fcomparison.png) [ ](architecture) Architecture 1. Frozen 26.4B MoE + Attention LoRA (r = 32): LoRA adapters (17.5M params) attached to self_attn.{q,k,v,o}_proj.{linear,gate_proj}; lm_head and vision_tower dropped for text decisioning. 2. ZeroWaste Layer17 Halting Gate (CoreGateHead, 1.2M params): After Loop 1 or Loop 2, a lightweight bilinear probe (\~0.05 ms) reads the Layer17 core output _before_ running exit layers 18–23. If calibrated confidence clears threshold, it skips the remaining loops and runs exit layers once. 3. TwoStage JointSchemaHead (6.0M params): _Stage 1 (Evidence Routing):_ <decide and every </opt token crossattend to 8 summary tokens of the input state. _Stage 2 (CrossOption Attention):_ Options and <decide selfattend to compare directly before bilinear pointer scoring. 4. MultiLoop Deep Supervision: Trained jointly across Loops 1, 2, and 3 (0.2·L1 + 0.3·L2 + 0.5·L3) using LabelSmoothed CrossEntropy + Brier Loss (0.5), then temperaturecalibrated on decisionv7/calibration. [ ](quickstart) Quickstart python from modeling import InklingDecisionModel model = InklingDecisionModel.from_pretrained("eltokh7/inkling2minidecision") out = model.decide( state="Customer email: 'My card was charged twice for order 4821 yesterday. Please refund.'", questions={ "route": { "type": "choice", "instructions": "Which team should handle this ticket?", "criteria": { "billing": "Duplicate charges, refunds, invoices", "tech": "Bugs, login issues, crashes", "sales": "Pricing, upgrades, quotes", }, }, "urgent": { "type": "noul", "instructions": "Does this require immediate escalation?", }, }, threshold=0.90, set to 1.01 to always run all 3 loops ) print(out) [ ](benchmarks) Benchmarks [ ](1loop1vsloop2vsloop3) 1\. Loop 1 vs. Loop 2 vs. Loop 3 Split $n$ Loop 1 (24L) Loop 2 (36L) Loop 3 (48L) L3 Brier L3 ECE Δ (L3 − L1) decisionv7/dev 1,468 81.95% 85.63% 85.63% 0.2056 0.0243 +3.68 pp decisionv7/test 1,440 82.29% 84.93% 85.56% 0.1944 0.0235 +3.27 pp hardv1/dev _(untrained OOD)_ 1,083 39.89% 60.85% 66.67% 0.4382 0.0522 +26.78 pp hardv1/test _(untrained OOD)_ 1,088 42.56% 58.18% 66.82% 0.4350 0.0750 +24.26 pp [ ](2zerowasteearlyexitrealcudalatencyv7test60questionsavg223tokensrtxpro6000blackwell) 2\. ZeroWaste Early Exit & Real CUDA Latency (v7/test, 60 questions, avg 223 tokens, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell) Headline numbers are median (p50) latency to match Kev’s benchmark convention (mean in parens). Mode (Merged LoRA + torch.compile, max Δp = 3.5e4) v7/test Acc v7/test L1 Exit hardv1/dev L1 Exit Median (p50) Mean Speedup vs. L3 (p50) :::::: Fixed Loop 3 (48L) 85.56%\ 0.0% 0.0% 136.8 ms 146.3 ms 1.00× Fixed Loop 2 (36L) 84.93% — — 100.2 ms 107.0 ms 1.37× Fixed Loop 1 (24L) 82.29% 100.0% 100.0% 65.6 ms 70.1 ms 2.09× Early Exit (τ = 0.90) 85.49% 54.2% 8.8% 81.4 ms 97.4 ms 1.68× Early Exit (τ = 0.85) 85.35% 60.0% 13.9% 79.6 ms 95.4 ms 1.72× Batched (bs = 8, causal_conv1d, L1 / L3) — — — 27.9 / 61.4 ms/q — 35.8 / 16.3 q/s _\Reverified on full decisionv7/test ($n=1{,}440$) after mergeandunload() \+ causalconv1d: 86.04% (1,239 / 1,440)._ [ ](limitationsnegativeresults) Limitations & Negative Results Extrapolating past Loop 3: Running 4 or 5 loops zeroshot degrades accuracy (63.5% → 59.5% → 46.1% on hardv1/dev) because Inkling2Mini was pretrained with fixed num_passes = 3. Raw date arithmetic: Without deterministic date_facts preprocessing, multiway date subtraction (hard_temporal_numeric) remains harder than multihop or tradeoff reasoning. items.title: Show HN: Hikari.ImGui, a pure C# re-implementation of Dear ImGui
items.desc: A pure, standalone C# re-implementation of the much-beloved and widely used immediate-mode GUI for 3D applications, Dear ImGui, targeting version v1.93.0-docking with zero native dependencies. Please feel free to use for your projects. Also available as a nuget package.
items.author: charm137
items.descZh: Dear ImGui 是深受喜爱且广泛使用的 3D 应用程序即时模式 GUI 的纯粹、独立的 C# 重新实现，目标版本为 v1.93.0，具有零本机依赖性。请随意用于您的项目。也可以作为 nuget 包提供。
